modules.name: VTC hard-rules checker
modules.effort: S: about 3 person-days as static JSON (rules 2, submission checklist 1); page and clause entry waits for registration
modules.design_question: Does the massing satisfy the VTC hard rules (height band, 9.0 non-residential FSR, site limits, below-grade transit link, submission format), and which results rest on an unread brief or on interpretation?
inputs: Layer0.Massing: tower and podium meshes with level planes
P01-M07 fsr_ledger: named ledger (default gross), three use-tier FSRs, residential area
P01-M09 site_frame (with ODP sub-area) and height table (CTBUH measures per tower)
P01-M02 sub-area table: residential_permitted, nonres_fsr_max
Layer0.SitePolygon: 79.2 m x 144.8 m block (project extract)
Layer0.TransitConnection: below-grade path plus station portal point placed from the brief's site plan
Per rule: brief page and clause (empty until S02 is opened); submission facts, editable

parameters.name: Brief-read state (S02 opened, page and clause per rule)
parameters.relationship: Brief unread -> every badge carries 'brief unread' and cannot turn green. Entering page and clause per rule is what lifts a rule from unverified to verified. Registration closes 29 Oct 2026.

parameters.name: Tower height H (architectural top, highest occupied floor, tip)
parameters.relationship: Height up -> storey count up at fixed floor-to-floor. Pass only inside the band, measured as set in P01-M09. Greater height raises view-cone and aviation exposure (P01-M04, P01-M05).

parameters.name: Band threshold in the brief's own unit
parameters.relationship: Brief unit is unread. 800-1000 ft = 243.84-304.80 m exactly, against 244-305 m. A tower at 304.9 m passes in metres and fails in feet; 243.9 m the reverse. Those slivers show amber 'unit-dependent'.

parameters.name: Which towers must lie in the band (all vs at least one)
parameters.relationship: Brief wording is 'one or more towers'. Default requires every tower in band; 'at least one' lets a shorter second tower pass. The switch moves pass/fail without moving the design; ask Buildner.

parameters.name: Counted non-residential floor area (tier chosen)
parameters.relationship: Counted area up -> non-residential FSR up in proportion. Site 79.2 x 144.8 m = 11,468 m2, so 9.0 FSR needs about 103,213 m2 (derived arithmetic, not a brief figure).

parameters.name: Ledger basis (gross vs zoning)
parameters.relationship: Gross counts every enclosed slab; the zoning ledger subtracts exclusions, so FSR falls. The brief's basis is unstated: M01 reads one named ledger (default gross) and flags when the two straddle 9.0.

parameters.name: Containment of above-grade volume (encroachment switch)
parameters.relationship: Coverage up -> fewer storeys for the same area but less open ground for public realm. Volume stays inside the block unless the switch allows air-space encroachment over streets, logged as a departure.

parameters.name: Below-grade transit connection: continuity and off-site length
parameters.relationship: A continuous path from a core to the station portal point, crossing under a street outside the polygon, meets 'connecting directly'. Off-site length up -> walking time and agreements up (MOBI packet).

parameters.name: Level bands holding public-tagged area
parameters.relationship: More bands with public-tagged area -> closer to 'public-facing uses extend vertically'. The brief says 'should', so this is a soft rule.

parameters.name: Residential permitted in the assumed ODP sub-area
parameters.relationship: Read from the M02 sub-area table for the sub-area M09 reports. Area A = 'no' (search summary, unopened): residential area above 0 then becomes a zoning departure sent to M08, not a nuance. Ask whether 9.0 mirrors Area A density.

parameters.name: Interpretation switches (height measure; all towers vs one; use tier; ledger)
parameters.relationship: Each switch moves pass/fail without moving the design, so each is logged as an assumption until Buildner answers (Q&A closes 3 Nov 2026).

parameters.name: Submission format rules (boards, size, MB limit, language, anonymity, deadline)
parameters.relationship: Breaking a rule is a submission risk, not a design result. Dates, English and anonymity are on the competition page; board count, A2 and the MB limit are not (10 MB per board or per submission?). Pointer to PRES.

modules.method: 1) Read the site polygon area (Shapely): 79.2 x 144.8 m = about 11,468 m2. 2) Take H_arch, H_occ, H_tip per tower from P01-M09; compare with the band stored in the brief's own unit, amber in the unit-dependent slivers. 3) Read one named ledger from P01-M07; FSR = tier area / site area for tiers 1-3. 4) Test above-grade mesh inside the polygon; encroachment logs a departure. 5) Graph path from a core node to the portal point, allowing off-site segments. 6) Count level bands with public tags. 7) Look up residential_permitted for the M09 sub-area; flag residential area above 0 in a 'no' sub-area. 8) Tick the submission checklist. 9) Emit one record per check: value, threshold, unit, state, switches, source id, brief-read state. No rule silently passes.

Jury link: urban_integration_10 (transit entrance), human_scale_40 (public uses up the tower); height and FSR are eligibility checks, not merit.

The public page states no height, FSR, site, board or jury-weight rule. The package may hold a site plan, 3D model and portal point. Geometry and tags only; failures are flags.

inputs: Static policy register (JSON): document, version, date, status, URL, clause, opened flag
Sub-area table typed from the Downtown ODP: residential_permitted, nonres_fsr_max, parking maximum, loading minimum
Higher Buildings policy-area flag and site height typed from the policy's Figure 1
Higher Buildings criteria checklist rows and reconciliation rows (typed)
Pointer rows handed to CLIM, ENER, MOBI, CULT and P01-M04/M05

parameters.name: Policy status and version date
parameters.relationship: Newer or under-review documents change which clause applies. Higher Buildings draft policies are due fall 2026-winter 2027 and the hearing spring 2027, so every result stays provisional until then.

parameters.name: Higher Buildings policy-area membership and site-specific height
parameters.relationship: Inside the area, allowed height differs by site (summaries cite about 700 ft on Georgia/Burrard/Granville, 425-500 ft at bridgeheads; unverified). The City quotes 600 ft (183 m) only for sites across from Bay Parkade. Outside: rezoning on merits.

parameters.name: Higher Buildings qualitative criteria (checklist, 6 rows)
parameters.relationship: Tests: excellence with enhanced Urban Design Panel review; public legacy or amenity; open space adding to the plaza network; no adverse microclimate, shadow or view impact; energy leadership; Council approval. Rows map to the jury weights; people judge them, code never scores them.

parameters.name: Downtown ODP sub-area table (residential_permitted, nonres_fsr_max)
parameters.relationship: The sub-area M09 reports selects permitted uses and the non-residential density cap, typed from the Downtown ODP. Area A is pre-filled 'no' (search summary, unopened). 'No' with residential area above 0 makes the brief's residential share a zoning departure.

parameters.name: FSR minimum and maximum, interpretive height, relaxation
parameters.relationship: Cap up -> permitted floor area up; above it, density needs bonus or CD-1 rezoning. ODP height provisions are interpretive and relaxable by the Development Permit Board, so zoning alone does not cap a supertall. Values typed from the PDF.

parameters.name: CBD land-use and job-space policy
parameters.relationship: 2009 Metro Core amendments raised non-residential density in Areas A, B, C1 and F and proposed removing residential from C1 and F (search summary, unopened). The sub-area decides whether VTC's 9.0 minimum mirrors it: ask Buildner.

parameters.name: Vehicle parking rule (minimum, maximum, retained minimums)
parameters.relationship: Council removed vehicle parking minimums for all uses citywide in June 2024 (downtown earlier). Maximum (Downtown ODP/Parking By-law) and accessible, visitor, bicycle, loading and passenger-loading minimums are typed. Fewer stalls allowed -> fewer below-grade levels (MOBI).

parameters.name: Transit-oriented area (context only)
parameters.relationship: The provincial rule bars residential parking minimums within 800 m of rapid transit. Vancouver's 2024 rule is wider, so TOA status does not set parking here. Kept as context for provincial minimum-density rules.

parameters.name: Large-sites rezoning policy trigger
parameters.relationship: Applies at a site of 8,000 m2 or more OR 45,000 m2 or more of new floor area (search summaries; adopted 25 Jul 2018, effective 1 Sep 2018, amended to Apr 2024). The block (11,468 m2; over 103,000 m2) meets both, so M08 gets obligation lines.

parameters.name: Other rezoning policies likely triggered
parameters.relationship: Green Buildings Policy for Rezonings, public art and bird-friendly guidelines each add submissions and design duties. Recalled by the reviewer, none opened: kept as unverified register rows.

parameters.name: Reconciliation and UNDRIP register rows
parameters.relationship: City UNDRIP Strategy (2022), City of Reconciliation framework (2014) and Nation engagement in rezonings are unverified rows pointing to CULT, so cultural context is not reduced to view protection. BC DRIPA s.3 opened; Sen̓áḵw is a reference precedent.

parameters.name: Zoning path (outright, relaxation, CD-1)
parameters.relationship: A CD-1 sets site-specific height, FSR and conditions; Bay Parkade's sets only a maximum height. Council's May 2023 direction sends non-conforming schemes to rezoning on merits. The path sets the scale of the benefits negotiation (P01-M08).

parameters.name: Precedent register (Bay Parkade rezoning, 27 Jul 2026, 7-3)
parameters.relationship: Council accepted three towers above policy heights with a large benefits package. Hotel plus residential, outside the policy area: evidence of a path for height beyond policy, not a rule and not a program precedent.

parameters.name: Pointer rows: shadow, wind, energy, public views, aviation
parameters.relationship: Rows name the governing documents handed on: shadow for named parks and plazas and wind comfort (CLIM), energy and emissions (ENER), cones (P01-M04), airspace (P01-M05). All unverified until read.

modules.name: Public view-cone checker
modules.effort: L: about 8-12 person-days, all v1: manual-parameter mode and ID crosswalk table 2-3 first; open-data ingestion 3-4; ray-casting 3-5
modules.design_question: Does the massing penetrate a protected public view cone (Queen Elizabeth Park or others), by how much, and does that trigger a Higher Buildings special review?
inputs: Layer0.Massing; highest physical point per tower from P01-M09 in the cone's datum
P01-M09 site_frame: assumed real block, ground elevation, vertical datum
City open data: 24 cone polygons (2D, modified 19 Oct 2026) as the in-force geometry, or cones in the brief package
Crosswalk table of cone IDs, hand-read from the Public Views Guidelines
Cone floors and azimuths typed from the Guidelines or a City View Cone Assessment (views@vancouver.ca)
Brief QE View image: five labelled existing tower heights (S56)
P01-M02 hb_policy_area flag; context massing, optional

parameters.name: Cone lower-boundary elevation at the site
parameters.relationship: Cone floor up -> allowable top up; allowable height = cone floor - ground elevation. Older documents suggest floors near 100-145 m (derived, unverified); 3.2.1 at one West End site was about 110.3 m (362 ft), historical and site-specific. The open data has no elevations.

parameters.name: Footprint position relative to the cone polygon
parameters.relationship: Footprint outside the polygon -> no penetration at any height; inside, every metre above the cone floor penetrates. Team check: sampled CBD points fell inside QEP cones 3.2.1-3.2.3 (2D, approximate); re-run on the real block.

parameters.name: View origin and subject
parameters.relationship: The origin is the camera for the skyline view; moving it changes every result. The four QEP polygons share a southern apex near 49.242 N (derived). The brief requires one skyline view from the QEP viewpoint.

parameters.name: Cone ID crosswalk and status
parameters.relationship: City data is in force (modified after 10 Jul 2024). 16 of 24 IDs match Storeys directly; 7 differ by suffix (E, G1, G2, J1, J2, 9.2, 20); cone 28 is in neither Storeys list; Storeys 12.2 has no record. Unmatched IDs stay 'unknown'.

parameters.name: Brief QE View reference image
parameters.relationship: Labelled existing towers: Butterfly 179 m, One Wall Centre 150 m, Living Shangri-La 201 m, Royal Centre 141 m, Harbour Centre 147 m. They calibrate the skyline view; they are not cone floors. The VTC band sits about 43-104 m above the tallest (derived).

parameters.name: Higher Buildings site status
parameters.relationship: Only select downtown Higher Buildings sites may enter QEP cone boundaries, through a special review (City page summary, unopened). Elsewhere penetration is not an option. The 2026 review does not revise protected views.

parameters.name: Ground elevation at the tower
parameters.relationship: Ground elevation up -> allowable height above grade down for a fixed cone floor (arithmetic). Taken from P01-M09 (City 2013 LiDAR DEM or typed).

parameters.name: Highest physical point tested (spire, plant, rig)
parameters.relationship: Rooftop plant, antennae and window-washing rigs count in a cone test, so penetration uses the highest physical point, not the CTBUH architectural top, in the cone's vertical datum.

parameters.name: Angular width of the tower from the origin
parameters.relationship: Width up -> more of the mountain skyline covered. No sourced acceptable-occlusion threshold found (see unresolved relationships).

metrics.name: Maximum penetration per cone
metrics.good: 0 m (all parts outside the cone)
metrics.method: Max over vertices and subdivided edges of (z_highest_point - cone_floor); 'unknown' when no floor is entered.
metrics.basis: Search summary of the Public Views Guidelines: all parts of a building should lie outside cone boundaries. PDF unopened.

metrics.name: Higher Buildings review trigger
metrics.good: no penetration, or penetration only at an identified Higher Buildings site with review planned
metrics.bad: penetration at a site not in the policy area
metrics.method: Penetration > 0 AND hb_policy_area flag from P01-M02.
metrics.basis: City page summary of the special review; policy area map unopened.

metrics.name: Cone status per cone and ID crosswalk
metrics.good: dataset dated after 10 Jul 2024 (City data, 24 cones) and every ID matched directly or by the hand-read crosswalk; status 'in force per City data'
metrics.bad: ID matched by string guess, an unmatched ID treated as retained, or an eliminated cone tested; 28 and 12.2 stay 'unknown'
metrics.method: Direct match (16), suffix candidates (7) confirmed by hand against the Guidelines, no match (1) flagged unknown; Storeys used for history only.
metrics.basis: Open data opened 21 Oct 2026; Storeys lists opened. r1: pre-2024 overstatement claim corrected. r2: ID matching against Storeys fails.

metrics.name: Cone-floor data present
metrics.good: floors and azimuths typed from a City document or the brief, with source id
metrics.bad: no floor values: result 'unknown' (grey hatched), never pass
metrics.method: Required field per cone; hypothetical-cone mode shows the floor in team-assumption colour and gives no pass/fail.
metrics.basis: Open dataset has polygons only; the block is hypothetical; the brief image gives no floors.

metrics.good: five labelled heights typed with source S56 and used only as context-tower references ('brief value')
metrics.bad: used as cone floors
metrics.method: Typed values; drawn as reference lines in section and panorama.
metrics.basis: Image viewed 21 Oct 2026; labels give feet and metres, measure and datum unstated.

metrics.good: 0% (team target)
metrics.bad: any occlusion; severity judged by people
metrics.method: Ray grid from the origin through the cone window; share of rays hitting the massing before the subject.
metrics.basis: Team preset; no sourced threshold.

modules.method: 1) Read the brief's QE View image: type the five labelled heights as 'brief value' context references (S56); they are not cone floors. 2) Check the brief package for cones, a real location or a portal. 3) If absent, assume a real block in P01-M09 or use hypothetical-cone mode (editable floor, no pass/fail). 4) Load the 24 City cones (2D) as in-force geometry; build the ID crosswalk by hand from the Guidelines; unmatched IDs are 'unknown'. 5) Type cone floors and azimuths from the Guidelines or a City View Cone Assessment (optional route). 6) Margin = z - cone_floor per vertex and subdivided edge; penetration = max. 7) Cast rays from the origin (three-mesh-bvh) against massing and context. 8) Render the origin view for PRES.

modules.name: Airspace height screening and obstruction marking
modules.effort: S-M: about 4-5 person-days (marking options and checklist 2; optional surface heightfields 2-3)
modules.design_question: Could federal aviation rules (YVR zoning, NAV CANADA procedures, harbour aerodromes) cap tower height, which marking and lighting options apply, and what must the team file or ask?
inputs: Highest physical point per tower, AGL and AMSL, from P01-M09 (roof additions count)
Site latitude/longitude from P01-M09
Typed coordinates: CYHC and the harbour heliport (sourced)
Optional heliport FATO position, approach azimuth, number of paths, performance class
Optional Transport Canada map or surface heights; crane height assumption

parameters.name: Highest physical point, AGL and AMSL
parameters.relationship: Top up -> more likely to penetrate an obstacle surface or instrument procedure and to need NAV CANADA mitigation. A roof mast counts toward height (CAR 601.23(2)). At Bay Parkade, City staff relayed that about 27 m (88 ft) may need cutting.

parameters.name: Obstacle status under CAR 601.23
parameters.relationship: Above 150 m AGL a structure is an obstacle, (1)(d); above 90 m AGL it is one within 6 km of an aerodrome's geographical centre or 3.7 km of a VFR route. Every VTC tower qualifies, so Standard 621 applies.

parameters.name: Distance to CYHC and the harbour heliport
parameters.relationship: Within 6 km, 601.23(1)(b) applies as well as (d). Team-derived: CYHC lies 0.8-2.5 km and the heliport (proxy at Waterfront Station) 0.4-1.9 km from Area A corners and sub-area centroids. Heliport coordinates and aerodrome status are unverified.

parameters.name: Configuration A: red (CL-810 steady plus CL-864 flashing), with paint
parameters.relationship: Red lights alone leave daytime paint required (s.4.2(2), s.5.2(1)(b)); on a building paint is a checkerboard (s.3.5(2)) or bands (s.3.5(3)). Consequence: painted crown pattern for SPAC and ECOL. Variant A' (CL-864 only) targets bird fatalities (s.5.4(1)).

parameters.name: Configuration B: medium-intensity white (CL-865), with paint
parameters.relationship: Paint is required above 150 m AGL with this system (s.4.2(3)(b) note, s.6.4(6)); a red-night, medium-white-day dual system too (s.4.2(5)(b)). Strobe-type CL-865 should not be used in urban areas (s.6.2 note): urban fit unproven; crown carries paint.

parameters.name: Configuration C: high-intensity white (CL-856/857), or dual with high-intensity white, no paint
parameters.relationship: Marking and other lights may be omitted at any height (s.4.2(4)(b), s.4.2(5)(b), s.3.7). May need an environmental evaluation near residences (s.2.4) and glare shielding (s.4.6). Consequence: bare crown, flashing white glare toward neighbours (SPAC, ECOL).

parameters.name: Who decides the final scheme
parameters.relationship: Transport Canada decides. Equivalent marking is approved by the Minister (s.2.1 note, CAR 601.24(2)); shielding only if the regional office assesses it (s.2.2(2)); notice 90 days before construction (s.2.5(1)). An option is a design choice, never an approval.

parameters.name: Distance and bearing to YVR runway strips
parameters.relationship: Under SOR/80-902 approach surfaces rise 1 m per 50 m to 15 km along runway centrelines; outer limits are described mainly in Richmond and along the Richmond-Vancouver boundary. No opened source puts downtown inside: applicability unknown, probably outside.

parameters.name: Proposed 2026 zoning extension
parameters.relationship: The July 2026 consultation adds an area (Vancouver north of the Fraser to English Bay, plus Burnaby) to the April 2024 proposal, so planes 'can safely arrive and depart'. Surface type and heights unpublished: if the CBD is inside, a surface may cap towers.

parameters.name: Existing taller buildings under the 2024 proposal
parameters.relationship: In the 2024 text, buildings existing at entry into force become legally non-conforming and may not be raised. The 2026 page is silent on this. 'Bump-out' exceptions were granted in five specific areas, Richmond among them.

parameters.name: Heliport surfaces (operator impact)
parameters.relationship: Standard 325: non-instrument approach 245 m at 6-10%, then 830 m at 16%; transitional 50% to 45 m. A building penetrating them affects the heliport's certification; it is not barred. Heliport, FATO and class are unknown.

parameters.name: Instrument procedures and harbour water aerodrome (CYHC)
parameters.relationship: NAV CANADA instrument-procedure obstacle clearance and floatplane and helicopter routes near Coal Harbour may bind height more than any zoning surface. Not modelled; carried as named unknowns for NAV CANADA to answer.

parameters.name: Assessment and notice timing
parameters.relationship: NAV CANADA attempts replies in 8-12 weeks, which 'can go up to 12 to 18 months pending necessary mitigations' in or around an airport; the letter is not a permit. Transport Canada notice is due 90 days before construction. Late filing risks floor cuts.

metrics.name: Obstacle and notice status (CAR 601.23-601.24, Standard 621 s.2.5)

metrics.bad: no notice logged, or notice after design freeze

metrics.bad: 'daytime marking always required above 150 m' applied to every option, or no option recorded

metrics.bad: test skipped, or heliport coordinates left as the proxy without a flag

metrics.basis: CYHC coordinates from Wikipedia (opened); heliport proxy at Waterfront Station; heliport aerodrome status unconfirmed.

metrics.bad: not applicable
metrics.method: Marker, not a threshold.
metrics.basis: Daily Hive: possible cut of about 88 ft from 1,034 ft (315 m) to 946 ft (288 m), relayed by City staff; no datum; constraint named only as 'federal aviation requirements'. r1: corrected from a 288 m screening flag.

metrics.name: NAV CANADA request timing
metrics.good: assessment requested at concept or pre-design stage (usual reply 8-12 weeks)
metrics.bad: requested after design freeze (up to 12-18 months pending mitigations near airports)
metrics.method: Checklist date logged by the user; no duration is predicted.

modules.method: 1) Take the highest physical point per tower from P01-M09 (AGL, AMSL). 2) Apply CAR 601.23: (d) above 150 m AGL; (b) above 90 m AGL within 6 km of an aerodrome centre; compute distances to CYHC and the harbour heliport from typed, sourced coordinates and list the triggered paragraphs. 3) Build the Standard 621 option table A, B, C: paint yes/no, clauses, crown and facade consequence; the user picks per tower; Transport Canada decides. 4) YVR zoning state defaults to 'outside current zoning (unverified)'; optional heightfield from user runway data. 5) 2026 surfaces stay 'unknown' until the map arrives. 6) Optional heliport flag from Standard 325 Table 4-1. 7) Checklist: Aeronautical Assessment Form at least 90 days before construction, NAV CANADA Land Use portal (separate), map request, DND note, crane assumption. Never 'approved'.

3D translucent surfaces with the tower when surfaces are known; penetrating mesh in red, legend 0-30 m
Map: block, CYHC and heliport with 6 km ring and distances

modules.human_judgment: Engaging NAV CANADA and Transport Canada; choosing among options A, B, C; trimming floors or repositioning; crown and lighting design; floatplane and helicopter routes; bird and glare impacts. No output is an aviation approval. Jury link: design_excellence_20 (crown, risk, cost of late cuts).
modules.limits: Downtown applicability of every zoning surface is unconfirmed. The 2026 surface heights and type are unpublished. Instrument procedures, CYHC data, heliport certification and the last 33,000 characters of Standard 621 were not read; Appendix C form fields not read. Clause details come from a summarising fetch. Screening only.

modules.name: Tower siting, separation and floor plate (report-only)
modules.effort: S: about 2-3 person-days; report-only, no grading until a City guideline is read
modules.design_question: What are the tower positions, floor plates, street walls and separations from on-site and neighbouring existing or approved towers, and which values would need justification once a guideline is read?
inputs: Layer0.Towers: floor-plate polygon per level, with use tags (residential, office, hotel)
Layer0.Podium and site edges (streets, lanes)
Context massing tagged existing or approved-not-built
P01-M09 site_frame: grid-to-true-north rotation

parameters.name: Tower-to-tower separation above podium, by use
parameters.relationship: Separation up -> daylight, privacy and sky view up, usable footprint down. A residential candidate of 24.4 m (80 ft) is recalled from Downtown South practice, unverified; office and hotel bands have no known value. Shown as a reference line only.

parameters.name: Cross-street separation
parameters.relationship: Towers across a street or lane: separation up with street width, usable plate down. No sourced value; computed from facade normals and reported, not graded.

parameters.name: Floor-plate area and width by level and use
parameters.relationship: Plate width up -> shadow width and wind-facing width up (CLIM packets), slenderness down. A residential candidate near 6,500 sq ft (about 604 m2) is recalled, unverified; no office or hotel cap found. Reference line only.

parameters.name: Street-wall (podium) height and setbacks
parameters.relationship: Podium height up -> stronger street wall and more shelter, less sky view from the street; setback up -> public realm and lane width up, plate area down. No sourced value for Georgia-type streets.

parameters.name: Distance to approved-not-built towers
parameters.relationship: Closer approved towers in the same height range -> separation shrinks and needs negotiation. Context must include approved towers such as Bay Parkade.

parameters.name: Grid-to-true-north rotation
parameters.relationship: Rotation decides which facade faces which compass direction in sun, wind and energy modules. Read from P01-M09; the brief's north arrow is rotated against the street grid.

metrics.name: Minimum tower-to-tower separation, residential bands (reference only)
metrics.good: reported; reference line 24.4 m (80 ft), editable; no grade
metrics.bad: no pass or fail until a City guideline is read; office and hotel bands 'unknown'
metrics.method: Minimum polygon distance and facade-normal distance per residential band above podium.
metrics.basis: Recalled residential guideline value; no City guideline could be opened. r2: report-only.

metrics.name: Residential floor-plate area (reference only)
metrics.good: reported; reference line about 604 m2 (6,500 sq ft), editable; no grade
metrics.bad: no pass or fail until a guideline is read
metrics.method: Slab polygon area per residential level.
metrics.basis: Recalled residential practice; not found in an opened source. r2: report-only.

metrics.name: Office and hotel floor-plate band
metrics.good: inside the team-entered band (no default supplied)
metrics.bad: outside the band; 'unknown' when no band is entered
metrics.method: Area per level from slab polygons.
metrics.basis: No sourced downtown floor-plate cap for office or hotel; team setting.

metrics.name: Context completeness
metrics.good: all existing and approved towers within the review radius (editable) are in the model
metrics.bad: any missing
metrics.method: Compare the context list with the City's approved-tower list.
metrics.basis: Brief context includes existing high-rises and approved towers.

modules.method: Slice each tower into level bands above the podium (Shapely) and tag each band by dominant use. For every tower pair, on-site and context, compute the minimum polygon distance and, for facing facades, the perpendicular distance along facade normals; keep the minimum per band. Compute floor-plate area, perimeter and bounding width per level, plus podium height and setbacks to lot lines and lanes. Compute each facade's grid and true bearing using the M09 rotation. Report values only: recalled residential candidates appear as editable reference lines, never as pass or fail, and office and hotel bands return 'unknown' unless the team enters a band. Return a pair matrix, cross-street distances and closest pairs. Approved-not-built towers are drawn hatched.

Elevation strip showing sky corridors between towers by level band
Floor-plate area bar chart by level and use with the team band shaded
Context towers coloured by status: existing, approved, proposed; approved-not-built drawn hatched
outputs: separation_matrix: pair x band distances, m
floor_plate_table: area, width per level and use
modules.human_judgment: Judging tower rhythm, views between towers and urban-design quality; deciding to depart from a guideline; anticipating the final form of approved neighbours. Jury link: human_scale_40 (sky corridors, daylight, street wall) and design_excellence_20.
modules.limits: No City guideline PDF on tower separation, floor plate or street wall could be opened. 24.4 m and 604 m2 are recalled residential candidates and must not be applied to office or hotel towers. Approved-but-unbuilt towers may change. Shadow, wind and daylight belong to CLIM.

modules.name: Program and FSR accounting
modules.effort: M: about 4 person-days core (gross ledger and three tiers 3, use-group tags 1); zoning ledger, exclusion presets and tornado chart are v1 (about 2-3)
modules.design_question: How much floor area counts toward total FSR and the 9.0 non-residential minimum under gross and zoning accounting, and how sensitive is compliance to use tiers, core allocation and exclusions?
inputs: Layer0 program-tagged slab polygons by level (or IFC spaces or mesh volumes), tags in by-law use-group codes
Site area (gross, optionally net of dedications)
Exclusion preset (editable list with clause ids), v1
Use-tier switch (tiers 1-3) and core/mechanical allocation switch

parameters.name: Accounting basis (gross vs zoning ledger)
parameters.relationship: Gross counts every enclosed slab; the zoning ledger subtracts listed exclusions, so FSR goes down. The brief's basis is unstated, so both ledgers are shown (zoning in v1) and one is named for P01-M01.

parameters.name: Exclusion rules (example set, v1)
parameters.relationship: Each enabled exclusion -> counted area down -> FSR down. CD-1 by-law examples (site-specific): parking, loading, mechanical at or below base surface; balconies to 8%; amenity to 1,000 m2; storage 3.7 m2 per unit; wall allowance 152 mm.

parameters.name: Use tier for the 9.0 minimum
parameters.relationship: Tier 1 Office; tier 2 adds Retail and Service uses (hotel pending); tier 3 adds Cultural and Recreational, Institutional and non-residential amenity. Residential amenity never counts. Each step raises non-residential FSR without changing the design.

parameters.name: Use-group tags (by-law vocabulary)
parameters.relationship: Layer0 tags carry by-law use-group codes (Office, Retail, Service, Cultural and Recreational, Institutional; others typed when read), so tiers here and the M02 permitted-use lookup share one vocabulary. Untagged area is an error, not zero.

parameters.name: Hotel classification
parameters.relationship: Hotel in tier 2 follows ordinary 'commercial' usage; the by-law is recalled (unverified) to list Hotel under Service Uses. Moving hotel in or out changes FSR by hotel area / site area. Confirm when the by-law is hand-read.

parameters.name: Core, circulation and mechanical allocation
parameters.relationship: Sharing core and mechanical area out to uses by served floor area raises office FSR; separate tags understate it. More mechanical floors -> gross area and height up; exclusions decide whether they count.

parameters.name: Site-area basis
parameters.relationship: Site area down (for example after dedications) -> FSR up for the same floor area. The brief gives only a gross block size.

metrics.name: Non-residential FSR, tier 1 (office only)
metrics.good: >= 9.0: passes under every reading
metrics.method: Office area / site area on the named ledger.
metrics.basis: 9.0 minimum from the brief extract (S02 unopened); tier definitions are team presets.

metrics.name: Non-residential FSR, tier 2 (office + retail + service incl. hotel; default claim reading)
metrics.method: Tier-2 area, core and mechanical shared out when the switch is on, / site area.
metrics.basis: Brief wording 'office, commercial' (extract). r1: corrected from a 'strict' reading labelled verified, with hotel excluded and core unallocated.

metrics.name: Non-residential FSR, tier 3 (all non-residential)
metrics.good: >= 9.0 (weakest reading)
metrics.bad: < 9.0: fails under every reading
metrics.method: Adds cultural/recreational, institutional, public and non-residential amenity; residential amenity excluded.
metrics.basis: Brief wording gap; team presets.

metrics.name: Interpretation gap (tier 3 minus tier 1)
metrics.good: gap does not change pass/fail
metrics.bad: tier 1 < 9.0 <= tier 3: result depends on interpretation
metrics.method: Three tiers run side by side.
metrics.basis: Wording gap in the brief; ask Buildner.

metrics.name: Total FSR (all uses)
metrics.good: reported only; no overall cap in the brief extract
metrics.bad: n/a (no cap)
metrics.method: All counted area / site area; Bay Parkade 27.4 (press, consolidated site) for orientation only.
metrics.basis: Brief extract (unopened); press figure from Storeys (opened).

metrics.name: Use-group tag coverage
metrics.good: 100% of slab area carries a by-law use-group code
metrics.bad: any untagged area
metrics.method: Tagged area / total area per level.
metrics.basis: Course rule: show work; code vocabulary named by the round-2 reviewer, by-law unopened.

metrics.name: Ledger reconciliation and exclusion documentation
metrics.good: level totals equal the ledger total, untagged area 0, 100% of exclusions carry a clause id and status
metrics.bad: any mismatch, untagged area or exclusion without a clause
metrics.method: Count documented / total; sum check.
metrics.basis: Course rule: show work and sources.

modules.method: Per level and tag, sum slab polygon areas (Shapely) or IfcSpace quantities (IfcOpenShell). Core: gross ledger (all enclosed floor area) by by-law use-group code. v1: zoning ledger (gross minus enabled exclusions, each with a clause id and status). When the switch is on, share core, circulation and mechanical area out to uses by served floor area. Divide by site area. Non-residential FSR for tier 1 (Office), tier 2 (adds Retail and Service uses including hotel) and tier 3 (adds Cultural and Recreational, Institutional, public and non-residential amenity); residential amenity is never counted. Run one-at-a-time sensitivity on each switch (v1). Reconcile the ledger with level totals; warn on untagged area. CD-1 exclusion values are shown as 'unverified examples', never as Downtown District rules.

Waterfall: gross GFA -> exclusions -> counted area -> tier 1, 2, 3 non-residential
FSR gauge with the 9.0 line; three tier markers and a ghost marker for the zoning ledger
Tornado chart of FSR change per switch (v1)

allocation_report: core and mechanical shares by use

parameters.name: Assumed real location of the block
parameters.relationship: Moving the block along the peninsula changes the ODP sub-area, view cones, airspace distances and ground elevation. Results in M01, M02, M04 and M05 hold only for the recorded assumption (team assumption until the brief gives a site).

parameters.name: ODP sub-area of the block
parameters.relationship: City boundary lines are polygonized, then a point-in-polygon test returns the label for M01 and M02. A wrong label moves residential_permitted and the FSR cap. Nested rings may be holes (check). Team-derived, boundaries approximate.

parameters.name: Ground elevation at the tower base
parameters.relationship: Ground elevation up -> top elevation above sea level up by the same amount for a fixed height above grade, so allowable height above grade under a cone or surface falls by that amount (arithmetic). City DEM cells are about 1 m.

parameters.name: Vertical datum of each dataset (CGVD28 vs CGVD2013)
parameters.relationship: A datum mismatch shifts every cone and aviation test by the offset: about 0.15-0.2 m near Vancouver (order of magnitude, secondary, unverified). Immaterial for 100 m margins, material near a cone floor: get NRCan GPS-H at the block before any margin under 1 m.

parameters.name: Grid-to-true-north rotation
parameters.relationship: Rotation up -> every facade bearing shifts by the same angle in sun, wind and energy modules. The brief's north arrow is rotated against the street grid; the value is read from the site plan.

parameters.name: Height measure (architectural top, highest occupied floor, tip, highest physical point)
parameters.relationship: Each measure adds or removes rooftop elements: CTBUH architectural top excludes antennae, while aviation height counts roof additions such as a mast (CAR 601.23(2)). Cone and aviation tests therefore use the highest physical point.

parameters.name: Reference level for CTBUH height
parameters.relationship: CTBUH measures from the lowest significant open-air pedestrian entrance. On a sloping downtown block a lower reference entrance -> reported height up by the difference, which can flip the band test.

parameters.name: Ground point that defines AGL for aviation
parameters.relationship: Standard 621 s.4.8(4) treats the tops of adjacent buildings as ground in congested areas, for counting light levels only; CAR 601.23 does not define AGL on a slope. Team assumption: the 150 m test uses the lowest adjacent grade (conservative) until Transport Canada confirms.

modules.method: 1) Record the assumed block (lat/long) or load the brief's site plan; mark it team assumption. 2) Pick a projected CRS (UTM zone 10, NAD83 CSRS) with pyproj; store the rotation between street grid and true north. 3) Look up the ODP sub-area from the pre-polygonized City boundaries (Shapely). 4) Type ground elevation (City DEM in v1); store the vertical datum of each dataset. 5) For each tower find the reference entrance Z, highest occupied floor, architectural top, tip and highest physical point. 6) Convert to AGL, AMSL and CTBUH; the 150 m obstacle test uses the lowest adjacent grade. 7) Publish site_frame and the height table; downstream modules call convert_height and never convert themselves.

flags.detail: Confirmed by Storeys and by the City open-data set of 24 cones (both opened); the City page is unopened. The scope text and older council documents still use the old name.

flags.claim: P01-M02: 'Sites inside the policy area, buildings up to 600 ft may be considered' is a verified, general threshold.
flags.correction: Policy heights are site-specific (policy Figure 1). 600 ft (183 m) is verified only for the sites immediately across the street from Bay Parkade; elsewhere it is unverified. M02 stores a lookup, status unverified until the PDF is read.
flags.detail: The City FAQ (opened 21 Oct 2026) says 'sites immediately across the street are within the policy area, where buildings up to 600ft (183 m) may be considered'; Bay Parkade itself lies outside the policy area. Summaries of the 2011 and 2018 policy (S08, S09, unopened) give about 700 ft on Georgia/Burrard/Granville and 425-500 ft at bridgeheads. Evidence: https://www.shapeyourcity.ca/higher-buildings/widgets/224666/faqs

flags.claim: P01-M05: The YVR zoning surface penetration metric is 'verified' for this tower.
flags.correction: Formula verified; applicability to downtown unknown (probably outside current zoning). The July 2026 proposal adds an area to the 2024 one and its surfaces are unpublished.
flags.detail: SOR/80-902 places the outer limits mainly in Richmond and along the Richmond-Vancouver boundary; approach surfaces follow runway centrelines. The April 2024 Gazette proposal describes a 4 km outer plane and names Richmond City Centre, Marpole, East Fraser Lands, Big Bend and Delta; downtown is not mentioned. Evidence: https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-80-902/FullText.html ; https://gazette.gc.ca/rp-pr/p1/2024/2024-04-27/html/reg5-eng.html

flags.claim: P01-M04: Pre-2024 cone data overstates restriction for the QEP tests.
flags.correction: Record retained, updated or eliminated per cone. For retained QEP cones 3.2.1-3.2.4 pre-2024 geometry may be unchanged: accept it with an 'unverified, confirm unchanged' badge. Do not test eliminated cones.
flags.detail: Storeys lists QEP views 3.2.1-3.2.4 as retained and none of the QEP views among the 11 updated cones; only 3.1 and 3.2.4a were eliminated. Global News reports a staff recommendation to reduce the bottom of the QEP cone without naming the view or saying it was adopted. City open data holds 24 polygons including 3.2.1-3.2.4. Evidence: https://storeys.com/vancouver-view-cones-policy-change/ ; https://globalnews.ca/news/10604105/protected-views-vancouver

flags.claim: P01-M05: The precedent screening flag is 288 m above grade.
flags.correction: 288 m is a display marker labelled 'height measure unstated' in the height ladder of P01-M08; it is not a threshold and not on M05's pass/fail cards.
flags.detail: Daily Hive gives 1,034 ft (315 m) with a possible cut of about 88 ft to 946 ft (288 m), attributed to City staff relaying NAV CANADA; no datum, no constraint beyond 'federal aviation requirements'. Specific to the Bay Parkade block. Evidence: https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/holborn-bay-parkade-vancouver-supertall-tower-nav-canada-federal-aviation

flags.claim: P01-M05: NAV CANADA replies take 12-18 months near airports.
flags.correction: Quote the conditional wording; base the metric on whether a request was logged at concept stage; add the Transport Canada Aeronautical Assessment Form (at least 90 days before construction) as a separate checklist item.
flags.detail: NAV CANADA 'attempts to respond within 8 to 12 weeks' and 'these times can go up to 12 to 18 months pending necessary mitigations' for a project in or around an airport. Transport Canada reviews obstacles to be marked and lit; the portal does not connect to it. Evidence: https://www.navcanada.ca/en/aeronautical-information/land-use-program.aspx

flags.claim: P01-M01 and P01-M07: The brief rules (244-305 m band, 9.0 non-residential FSR, site size, transit entrance) are 'verified'.
flags.correction: Downgraded to unverified (the two core metrics are marked false_assumption_corrected). The team registers by 29 Oct 2026, downloads the brief and cites page and clause for each rule.
flags.detail: Their only source, S02, is opened=false because the PDF is email-gated. The competition page (S01) states dates, organisers and prizes but no height, FSR, site, transit or board rules. The packet's convention forbids 'verified' without an opened source. Evidence: https://architecturecompetitions.com/vancouvertallchallenge

flags.claim: P01-M08: Mapping benefits to 'cash CAC' is a verified Vancouver Charter statutory mapping (ss. 565.1, 565.13).
flags.correction: Five separate categories: in-kind condition (s.565(1)(f.1), s.565.17), payment in lieu of density-bonus conditions (s.565.13), DCL (s.523D), ACC (s.523E, in-kind s.523M), and policy-based CAC (negotiated; status 'policy, unverified').
flags.detail: s.565.1 sets base plus higher density for amenities and s.565.13 lets a by-law offer payment in place of conditions at estimated capital cost; neither sets Vancouver's negotiated rezoning CAC, which follows City policy (unopened). ACCs cannot apply where a DCL may be imposed (s.523I(2)) or duplicate amenity conditions (s.565.1(2.1)). Evidence: https://www.bclaws.gov.bc.ca/civix/document/id/complete/statreg/vanch_28 ; https://www.bclaws.gov.bc.ca/civix/document/id/complete/statreg/vanch_256

flags.claim: P01-M08: Bay Parkade is a usable benchmark for a VTC employment-led tower.
flags.correction: Use Bay Parkade only for height beyond policy, aviation risk and benefit scale. Show a precedent-fit note (program, policy-area status, height measure). Never use it for the program mix or the 9.0 non-residential test.
flags.detail: Bay Parkade is a hotel tower plus residential towers and a social housing tower, with no office (Daily Hive, Storeys), and lies outside the Higher Buildings policy area (City FAQ). Storey counts conflict: Storeys 63 (north), 79 (south), 68 (hotel); Daily Hive 68 for the hotel; Construction Canada 79 for the hotel. Evidence: https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/holborn-vancouver-western-canada-tallest-tower-bay-parkade-redevelopment-approved ; https://storeys.com/holborn-vancouver-supertall-council-approved/

flags.claim: P01-M05 and key findings: Above 150 m AGL daytime marking is always required for every VTC tower, and strobe-type lights are not recommended in urban areas.
flags.correction: Day marking is required above 150 m AGL with red and with medium-intensity white (CL-865) systems, but may be omitted with high-intensity white, or dual systems using high-intensity white, at any height. High-intensity white near residences may need an environmental evaluation and glare shielding. The urban strobe note covers CL-865 units. Transport Canada decides the final scheme.
flags.detail: Standard 621 s.4.2(3)(b) note, 4.2(4)(b), 4.2(5)(b), 3.7, 6.4(6), 6.2 note, 2.4, 4.6, 2.2, 2.1 note (summarising fetch of the Transport Canada page, 21 Oct 2026; clause text still to be quoted). r1 also cited s.12.1 for birds; that note concerns wind turbines (building text is s.5.4(1)). Evidence: https://tc.canada.ca/en/corporate-services/acts-regulations/list-regulations/canadian-aviation-regulations-sor-96-433/standards/standard-621-obstruction-marking-lighting-canadian-aviation-regulations-cars

flags.claim: P01-M02: Inside a transit-oriented area residential parking minimums are zero, but commercial parking may still be required (TOA is the operative parking rule).
flags.correction: Vancouver removed minimum vehicle parking for all land uses citywide in June 2024 (downtown earlier). Accessible, visitor, bicycle, loading and passenger-loading requirements remain; Downtown ODP maximums apply. TOA status is context only.
flags.detail: CTV (opened) confirms the unanimous 26 Jun 2024 vote; scope and effective date (30 Jun 2024) come from a search summary of the council report (unopened); the BC TOA page covers residential parking only. Evidence: https://www.ctvnews.ca/vancouver/article/vancouver-council-votes-to-eliminate-minimum-parking-requirements-city-wide ; https://council.vancouver.ca/20240626/documents/cfsc2.pdf ; https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/housing-tenancy/local-governments-and-housing/housing-initiatives/transit-oriented-areas

flags.correction: Treat the City open data (modified 19 Oct 2026) as the in-force geometry; build a crosswalk from the Public Views Guidelines (hand-read); use Storeys for history only; unmatched IDs are 'unknown'.

flags.claim: P01-M02/M08: The large-sites policy thresholds (0.8 ha / 45,000 m2) and the CBD residential restriction are reviewer recollections with no sourced evidence.
flags.correction: Both have public evidence, seen only as search summaries because City hosts return 403: the policy applies at a site of 8,000 m2 or more OR 45,000 m2 or more of new floor area; a 2022 Council report says residential use is not permitted in DODP Area A. The VTC block meets both triggers; Area A residential is a departure.

Evidence: https://guidelines.vancouver.ca/policy-rezoning-sustainable-large-developments.pdf ; https://guidelines.vancouver.ca/bulletins/R019.pdf ; https://council.vancouver.ca/20220705/documents/r9.pdf ; https://council.vancouver.ca/20090421/documents/ph1summary.pdf

flags.claim: YVR airport zoning caps downtown tower heights.
flags.detail: Current SOR/80-902 outer limits are described mainly in Richmond and along the Richmond-Vancouver boundary; no source says downtown is inside. Transport Canada's July 2026 proposal adds an area covering much of Vancouver north of the Fraser, and Burnaby, to the April 2024 proposal; heights and surface type for it are unpublished. Bay Parkade shows aviation can still cut height, relayed only as 'federal aviation requirements'.

flags.claim: Higher Buildings Policy height range is about 550-700 ft in the CBD.
flags.detail: From search summaries of the 2011 and 2018 versions; the City FAQ (opened) gives 600 ft only for the sites across from Bay Parkade. The adoption date differs between summaries (22 Apr vs 6 May 1997); amendments cited: 2003, 2011, 2018. The Shape Your City policy link is a download stub: hand-read the PDF.

flags.claim: Do hotel, cultural/civic and public-oriented floor area count toward the 9.0 non-residential minimum, and on which ledger (gross or zoning)?

P01-M01 and P01-M07 show three tiers side by side (Office; plus Retail and Service incl. hotel; plus Cultural and Recreational, Institutional, public and non-residential amenity), residential amenity never counted. Ask Buildner before 3 Nov 2026; registration closes 29 Oct 2026.

flags.detail: Recalled from Downtown South practice, residential only; not found or opened. Must not be applied to CBD office or hotel towers. r2: P01-M06 is v1 and report-only, with these as editable reference lines, never graded.

flags.detail: Derived from older documents: 322.8 ft (1997, 1989 cones), 332 ft (2020), 123-143 m (1070 Barclay) and, r2, about 110.3 m (362 ft) for 3.2.1 at one West End site (2022 search summary, replacing 361 ft); all unopened and pre-2024 or site-specific. flags.detail: r2: search summary gives 8,000 m2 OR 45,000 m2 of new floor area (same 0.8 ha), adopted 25 Jul 2018, amended to Apr 2024; PDF unopened. Both triggers met by the block.
